description: The Korean Wave, or Hallyu, is usually dated to 1997, when Chinese state broadcaster CCTV aired the Korean drama "What is Love" (1991-92), an unlikely hit that is often credited as the phenomenon's starting point. Almost three decades later, the industry that emerged from it has become one of Korea’s most closely watched exports, with dramas, K-pop, webtoons and games driving revenue growth and global success, and spilling over into related industries such as tourism, beauty, food and fashion. description: Celebrities build their careers in the public eye, but in South Korea, the public's interest in their lives often extends well beyond their work — and increasingly into their homes. When a celebrity buys or sells a property, entertainment reports routinely detail where it is, how much it cost, what type of home it is, whether the celebrity borrowed money to buy it and how much they may have gained from the transaction. description: Visitors expecting Georg Baselitz's famous upside-down figures at his first Korean museum retrospective are greeted instead by a picture of cattle, hung front and center right upon entering the galleries. description: When foreign musicians look to Korea for inspiration, K-pop is often the obvious starting point. But not everyone is listening to chart-topping idols. description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi sent an offering to a war shrine seen as a symbol of Japan's imperialistic past Saturday to mark the country's 1945 surrender in World War II. Takaichi sent the offering to Tokyo's Yasukuni Shrine in her capacity as president of the Liberal Democratic Party without visiting the shrine in person. Before taking office, Takaichi had visited the shrine on Aug. 15 every year, but she is believed to have refrained from doing so as prime minister in consideration
title: Japan PM sends offering to Yasukuni Shrine, refrains from visit
